meta.method: Targeted review of titles, abstracts, publication types and linked notices for all 36 PubMed records in the August Figure 3 ledger, retrieved through Europe PMC. Study-setting labels and summaries were checked against those abstracts. This is not a systematic literature search or a full-text quality assessment. Published correction notices are linked; their full contents have not been assessed. Eight additional connections were selected to broaden human disease coverage, including six families absent from the original selection. Ten primary-study titles and abstracts, publication types and linked notices were checked through Europe PMC. These are newly added records, not newly published studies. This targeted extension is not exhaustive and does not update the August resource audit.

Patient blood-cell populations with defective GPI anchoring shared a somatic PIGA mutation, linking an acquired clonal blood disorder to loss of surface GPI-anchored proteins.

T cells derived from adult celiac lesions preferentially recognized deamidated gliadin, supporting a role for tissue transglutaminase in forming the recognized epitopes.

A study of 25 men linked somatic UBA1 variants to adult-onset inflammatory disease, reduced cellular ubiquitylation and impaired activity of a cytoplasmic UBA1 isoform.
The original cohort and tested variants do not represent all patients with VEXAS. Somatic mutation evidence is not an inherited-risk estimate or proof of benefit from altering ubiquitination.

Biochemical studies identified FAM20C as a kinase for secreted biomineralization proteins; tested Raine syndrome variants impaired its localization and kinase activity.
These studies address the biochemical function of a disease-associated enzyme. They are not clinical trials and do not establish which individual substrate changes account for each patient feature.
